newsitem.title: USA: Enron, utility unfazed by extended reviews.
newsitem.headline: Enron, utility unfazed by extended reviews.

text.p: Enron Corp and Portland General Corp on Thursday said they were unfazed by a decision by Oregon regulators to extend the schedule for reviewing the companies' planned merger.
"We are confident that the merits of this merger will be recognized and we look forward to its approval in March," Enron Chairman Ken Lay said.
The Oregon Public Utility Commission delayed until March 17 its decision on $3.2 billion merger of the Houston-based energy conglomerate with the Oregon utility.
Enron shares fell 2-3/4 to 41-3/8 in New York Stock Exchange trading on the news, while Portland General shares were off 2-5/8 at 39-1/4, also on the Big Board.
"We are terribly disappointed by the overreaction of the market to this news," Lay said.
The companies said no new issues were raised by intervenors, and discovery proceedings will close on December 20.

The Oregon commission's staff recommendation on the merger is now due by January 16, 1997, a settlement conference was slated for January 22-24, and a final staff recommendation is due by January 31, the companies said.
